description: Argus Array survey bands for the current hardware: beta (Chroma CT446-162bp, about 360-526 nm) and rho (Chroma CT699-259bp, about 567-826 nm), on PlaneWave DeltaRho 280 (DR280) telescopes with Sony IMX461 CMOS sensors. Each published curve is filter x DR280 optics x detector QE, without atmosphere. The filter, optics and QE are served as separate components: filter variants 'production' (default) and 'addem', and the DR280 optics, which ADDem and production share.
facility_description: The Argus Array, built at the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill, is an array of small telescopes designed to observe the entire accessible sky at high cadence (Law et al. 2022, PASP 134, 035003; Law et al. 2024, Proc. SPIE 13094, 130941W). The 2022 paper describes an earlier hardware design (g-band and wide g+r filters, IMX455 sensors, 203 mm f/2.8 telescopes) that has since been replaced; the current hardware is DR280 telescopes with IMX461 sensors and the beta and rho bands.
notes: Published curves: filter x optics x QE of the default components, composed by SED_Tools (linear interpolation on the merged grid; zero outside a component's tabulated range), so composing the defaults reproduces them exactly. Filter variants: 'production' (default): argus_sim's argus_beta_ct446.csv and argus_rho_ct699.csv (commit 37a25ebb), Chroma's design curves averaged over the DR280 beam. 'addem': the ADDem (Argus Deep-field Demonstrator) filters: the same CT446-162bp beta filter, with the production curve, and the earlier CT692-276bp red filter rho0 in the rho band, from the filter_beam column of synthref's synthref_response_rho.csv. synthref's README calls that column 'rho0 CT692-276 theory, AOI n_eff 1.6', while its code defaults say the measured lot 452749; which it is is unresolved. ADDem's own calibration curves (synthref, hdps) used a beta curve with a provisional +5 nm red edge; that curve is archive-only, so 'addem' beta equals 'production' beta. Composed with the default optics and QE, 'addem' rho reproduces synthref's own rho response (R_noatm) to 1e-6. Optics: the DR280 vendor-coating model dr280_vendor_s2s2 (hdps addem_optics.csv), which ADDem and production share: two 'supplier 2' enhanced-aluminium mirrors digitised by eye from the vendor coating sheet, three CDGM corrector lenses and six AR surfaces at 0.5%; no window, since the filter substrate is in the filter curve and the sensor cover glass in the QE. It is a model; no measured optics exist. QE: Sony IMX455, digitised from the datasheet (version and figure not recorded). The deployed sensor is the Sony IMX461; no IMX461 QE curve is available, so the IMX455 curve stands in, as in every Argus pipeline. No atmosphere is published or offered: the only atmosphere in the Argus repositories (pachon_modtran_atm_aerosols.txt) is LSST's Cerro Pachon MODTRAN model at airmass 1.2 (syseng_throughputs siteProperties/pachonModtranAtm_12_aerosol.dat), labelled airmass 1.0, and is not the Argus site. Detector type energy per the Argus team (N. Miller, 2026-10-27); argus_sim's throughput.py describes the product as a photon-rate response. Caveat: argus_rho_ct699.csv (2026-09-25) may use an earlier single-field-angle beam model rather than the field average used for argus_beta_ct446.csv (2026-10-21); the difference is probably small. Sources: the production filters and the QE are public (argus-hdps/argus_sim, MIT). The optics curve and the rho0 curve are not: addem_optics.csv is only on unmerged branches of the private argus-hdps/hdps repository, and the rho0 curve only in argus-hdps/synthref, now removed from GitHub. NJM is their source; SED_Tools' builder (component_sources/argus.py) stops and points to NJM without them. All inputs are archived in source_evidence/filters/2026-10-27-argus on NJM (manifest.json gives each file's URL or origin, retrieval time and SHA-256). Archive-only, available on request: the 22 measured Chroma production-lot curves (order SO448371: 8 beta, 14 rho), the legacy design-study bands (r, i, A, r+i, i+z, r+i+z and the 560-825 nm rho box) and the provisional red-edge beta curve. Credit: the filter beam averages, the DR280 optics model and the IMX455 digitisation are by Hank Corbett (UNC). Nill's earlier curves, which his MESA projects use, are Argus/System.

licence.scope: Software licences of the source repositories, not data licences written for the curves. The MIT licence (argus-hdps/argus_sim, public, commit 37a25ebb) covers argus_beta_ct446.csv, argus_rho_ct699.csv and imx455_qe.csv: the production filter components and the QE. The BSD 3-Clause licence (argus-hdps/hdps, private; LICENSE on main) covers addem_optics.csv, the default 'dr280' optics component. Both are in the published curves. No licence file covers the other input: the rho0 curve (filter variant 'addem') is from argus-hdps/synthref, which has no licence file and is removed from GitHub.
